name: com.anaella/mcp
title: Anaella
description: One API for agents: web, SEO, media and doc tools, plus your email, calendars, ads and social.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List every account connected to Anaella (mailboxes, calendars, Google Sheets, Google Drive, Slack, Search Console, Analytics, ads accounts, Business Profile, Stripe, PayPal, social networks…) with its `platform` and `features`. An account id is the `accountId` of the other tools: pass it in do inputs when several accounts of a kind are connected, and as `channels` in social.post.create ("publish" accounts only). Pass `feature` to filter. Free.

feature.description: Only accounts with this feature: publish (can post), analytics (can report), inbox (messages, comments, reviews), tools (usable in do)

tools.name: connect_account
tools.description: Connect an account. Three ways, by what you pass. (1) `credentials`: for accounts that sign in with a form instead of a browser (an IMAP/SMTP mailbox, Bluesky, Telegram, Inkwire, a WordPress or Ghost website, PayPal, n8n, an MCP server with a token, Bing Webmaster Tools, a Stripe restricted key) it connects now and returns the new channel (use its id as accountId). Anaella checks the login first and stores nothing if it fails; the error says what to fix. Use only details the user gave you. platform "phone" BUYS a number: $3.00 a month from the Anaella balance, so get the user's yes first. (2) No `credentials`: returns a link (`url`) for a person to open and sign in themselves, which is how Google, Microsoft, Slack, Meta and every other browser sign-in connects, and how a user who would rather not share a password with you enters it. With `externalUserId` and `returnUrl` the link is for one of your own end users (single use, 30 minutes; their browser returns to returnUrl with ?status=connected&channelId=… or ?status=error&code=…; returnUrl must be allowed under Settings → API keys → Connect). Without them it is the organization's own connect page. The account is not connected until they finish. Afterwards call it with do (e.g. gsc.queries.list).

platform.description: The account type. With credentials: imap (any mailbox), bluesky, telegram (a bot), inkwire (an Inkwire site), wordpress (a self-hosted WordPress site), ghost (a Ghost site), paypal, n8n, mcp (an MCP server), bing-webmaster (Bing Webmaster Tools), phone (buys a number), stripe (restricted key). Without credentials, a link for a browser sign-in: social networks (instagram, facebook, threads, x, linkedin, linkedin-page, tiktok, youtube, pinterest, reddit, mastodon), Google (gmail, google-calendar, google-sheets, google-drive, google-search-console, google-analytics, google-ads, google-business-profile), Microsoft (outlook), meta-ads and slack.

credentials.description:
Omit for a link. The sign-in fields for this platform (all strings). Required, then (optional):
imap: email, password (an app password where the provider has them), imapHost, smtpHost (imapPort 993, smtpPort 465, username = email, name)
bluesky: handle, appPassword
telegram: botToken, chatId
inkwire: siteUrl, apiKey, name
wordpress: siteUrl, username, applicationPassword (Users > Profile > Application Passwords; the site must use HTTPS), name
ghost: siteUrl, adminApiKey (id:secret, from Settings > Integrations > Add custom integration), name
paypal: clientId, clientSecret, email (currency, name, environment)
n8n: baseUrl, apiKey (name, webhookUrl)
mcp: url = the server's public https address (token, headerName such as X-API-Key, name). A server with its own sign-in page (Notion, Linear) needs no token: omit credentials and give the user the link.
bing-webmaster: apiKey from Bing Webmaster > Settings > API access (name)
phone: country US or CA (areaCode, name). Buys a number.
stripe: apiKey = a restricted key rk_live_… (name).

externalUserId.description: Your own id for the end user; omit for the organization's own account. Required with returnUrl for an end user's link.

returnUrl.description: For an end user link only: URL the person is sent back to after connecting. Required with externalUserId when you pass no credentials.

tools.name: remove_account
tools.description: Disconnect an account (accountId from list_accounts): deletes it and its stored login, revokes Anaella's access at the provider, and a phone number is released (it can't be bought back). An account with post history is archived instead, keeping its posts. Irreversible: name the account to the user and get their yes first.

accountId.description: The account to remove (id from list_accounts)

externalUserId.description: Your own id for the end user; omit for the organization's own account

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search Anaella's capability catalog by what you want to do. Everything Anaella does is in it: email (read, search, send on Gmail, Outlook / Microsoft 365 or any IMAP mailbox: email.messages.list, email.message.get, email.attachment.read, email.message.send), calendar (Google or Outlook: calendar.availability.get, calendar.event.create), Google Sheets (sheets.read, sheets.append…), Google Drive and Docs (drive.files.search, drive.file.read, docs.create), Slack (slack.channels.list, slack.messages.list, slack.message.send), watches that report new items (watch.create, watch.events.list), automations where an AI agent handles new items with your instructions, writes waiting for approval (automation.create, automation.action.decide), SEO (gsc.*), Analytics (analytics.report), Meta and Google Ads, Google reviews, social comments (social.comments.*), social posting and analytics (social.post.create, social.posts.list, social.post.analytics…), media (media.upload, image generation, stock), web search and page reading. Examples: "read my inbox", "free time tomorrow", "append a row to a sheet", "schedule a post", "automate replies to new emails". Returns ids, summaries, prices and whether the account is connected. Free. Input: q (what you want to do; query works too) and category, nothing else. The best matches include their input schema (`input`): do the one you picked straight away. Call explain only when `inputOmitted` is true or you need its description or output schema.

q.description: What you want to do, in plain words, e.g. "update cells in a google sheet". Without it (and without a category) you get the list of families, not tools

category.description: Only this family, e.g. email, calendar, ads, seo, media, social, stripe; "raw" also lists raw pass-through calls

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Get a capability's input and output JSON Schema, price and description. Free. Call before do.

tools.name: do
tools.description: Run a catalog capability (id from find, input matching its explain schema), e.g. id "email.messages.list" with input { "query": "is:unread" } to read a connected mailbox. Pass `accountId` in the input when several accounts of that kind are connected. Most capabilities are free; paid ones bill the balance. Some capabilities have a daily quota (quotaPerDay in find/explain); beyond it the call fails with 429 rate_limited and resetAt. Async capabilities return a queued job: pass wait=true to block until it finishes, or poll with job.

input.description: Input object per the explain schema

wait.description: Wait for an async job to finish (default false: returns the job; poll it with get_job)

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Get the status, output, error and cost of a job returned by do. Free.

tools.name: preview_post
tools.description: Show the user a preview of a post before it is published: how it reads on each account, with its length against the platform limit, its media and its time, and a Publish (or Schedule) button. Pass `post`: the exact input you would give social.post.create. Call it instead of asking "shall I publish?" in text. The user publishes from the preview, and you are told when they do: never call social.post.create yourself for that post afterwards. If they ask for changes, call preview_post again with the new input. Free.

post.description: The social.post.create input: channels, text, media, when, overrides…
